definitions.ISSUE-01: When the basic two-year limitation period started running on the client's negligence claim against its accountant: discovery of the claim under the Limitations Act, 2002, assessed on the Grant Thornton plausible-inference standard, not the date the statements were negligently prepared.
definitions.PROP-01: A proceeding shall not be commenced in respect of a claim after the second anniversary of the day on which the claim was discovered (the basic limitation period).
definitions.PROP-02: A claim is discovered on the earlier of the day the claimant first knew the s 5(1)(a) matters (injury, causation, identity of the defendant, and that a proceeding is an appropriate remedy) and the day a reasonable person with the claimant's abilities and circumstances first ought to have known of them; s 5(2) presumes knowledge on the day of the act or omission unless the contrary is proved.
definitions.PROP-03: A claim is discovered when the plaintiff has knowledge, actual or constructive, of the material facts upon which a plausible inference of liability on the defendant's part can be drawn - more than mere suspicion or speculation, but less than certainty of liability or knowledge of every constituent element.
definitions.CONCLUSION-01: The basic limitation period runs from 2024 discovery (subject to the s 5(2) presumption being rebutted), so the Limitations Act, 2002 ss 4-5 and Grant Thornton must rank first and second.
definitions.CLAIM-01: The Limitation Act, SBC 2012, c 13 governs the limitation period for this Ontario claim (wrong jurisdiction).
definitions.CLAIM-02: The Real Property Limitations Act supplies the limitation period for a professional-negligence claim about financial statements (wrong Ontario statute; it governs land and rent).
definitions.CLAIM-03: R. v. Oakes or the Food and Drug Regulations bear on when the limitation period started running.
